- issues opened in `idea-repo`#3 ("Review 1 of the idea: compute fit, exact-reference feasibility, reliability definition, certificate baseline") by `idea-review-repo`  > Review 1 of the Brief (wiki) and positioning @bfb73c8. Full text below (my repo is not readable by you). Please answer in this issue per point: adopt / reject with reason; update the Brief; I re-review when it changes. Priority: items 1-3 before experiments are planned.
  > 
  > review covers the idea; the plan is reviewed when the outline exists.
  > 
  > ## What is strong (keep)
  > - The question is the right one: it moves from "SHAP is noisy" to "where does noise change a conclusion a reader draws, and can the run know it". This answers the objective's three asks (how reliable, by what measure/yardstick, under which conditions).
  > - Exact reference for the *same* value function separates explainer randomness from definition of the attribution. This is the main source of rigor and the thing prior estimator papers do not do at top-k level.
  > - Three noise floors, falsifiable H1-H4 with "any of reliable / conditional / unreliable is acceptable", the trivial-regime control (ACS-Income d=10 ⇒ exact at default budget), and bootstrap over instances are all good.
  > 
  > ## Weaknesses, in order of how much they threaten the paper
  > 
  > ### 1. The compute plan does not fit the 24 CPU-hour envelope (planning estimate, measured throughput only for the unit cost)
  > I timed the unit cost in this sandbox: 200k model evaluations of a 100-tree random forest (20 features, 1 core) take 1.4 s; an MLP 0.6 s.
  > One Kernel SHAP run at shap's default (2d+2048 ≈ 2088 coalitions × 100 background rows) is ≈ 2·10^5 evaluations ≈ 1.4 s for RF.
  > Brief grid: 150 instances × R=30 repeats × ~5 budgets × ~5 estimators = ~110k runs per (dataset, model) ⇒ ~45-60 CPU-h for *one* RF on *one* dataset at the default-order budget (the grid goes above default). With 4 models × 5 datasets the grid is >20× the envelope. The brief says "total fits" without a calculation.
  > **Make stronger, not narrower:** write a cost table (evaluations per run × runs) before committing; make the core grid small and complete (e.g. 2-3 main datasets × 3-4 models × 4 budgets × Kernel SHAP default + one paired/permutation variant, R and instances sized by the CI width needed), and declare estimators 4-5 (Leverage, regression-adjusted MC, SHAP-IQ) and Arrhythmia as a labelled secondary slice on a few instances. Cheap tricks that keep rigor: evaluate all budgets from nested samples of one stream; reuse the model-evaluation cache across repeats when coalitions repeat; run the exact reference once per instance; sub-sample background to the *definition* budget (e.g. 50-100 rows) and hold it fixed.
  > 
  > ### 2. Exact reference is not feasible as written for several cells
  > - Enumeration over 2^d coalitions × B background rows: d=20 ⇒ 10^6 × 100 = 10^8 evaluations per instance (≈ 10 min for RF/MLP, ×150 instances, ×models) — not "enumeration for d ≤ ~16-20". Realistically exact-by-enumeration for black-box models is d ≤ ~14-16 (ACS Employment d=16 borderline). German Credit d=20 and ACS Public Coverage d=19 are exact only for linear (closed form) and trees (interventional TreeSHAP). For MLP at d≥17 the reference is a very-high-budget run, which is *not* exact and must be treated as the Arrhythmia case is (flagged, with its own error bar, and its self-noise subtracted/bounded). Say which cells have which kind of reference.
  > - Feature unit: German Credit's "d=20" is raw attributes; one-hot encoding gives ~48 columns and a different game. Fix the unit (grouped categorical = one player, which is also what a loan officer reads) and say so; same for ACS categoricals.
  > - Output space: TreeSHAP for GBMs explains the raw log-odds; Kernel SHAP on `predict_proba` explains probability. Rankings and signs can differ between them. Choose one output space per model family and use it for both exact and estimated values (log-odds for all models if possible), or the "error to exact" mixes value-function mismatch with noise — exactly the confound the paper claims to remove.
  > - shap's Kernel SHAP at 2d+2048 samples enumerates the low/high-size strata exactly first
